thought: The user wants me to act as an intake analyst for pi-rsi and produce JSON only matching a specific schema. Let me analyze the Spaceship Titanic problem based on the provided information.

structuredOutput.understanding: This is the Kaggle Spaceship Titanic binary classification task: predict whether each passenger was Transported (True/False) from tabular passenger features. Training data has 8693 labeled rows with HomePlanet, CryoSleep, Cabin, Destination, Age, VIP, amenity spend columns, Name, and the Transported label; the public test set has 4277 unlabeled rows in the same feature schema. PassengerId encodes group membership (gggg_pp) and Cabin encodes deck/number/side, so feature engineering and leakage-aware validation matter. A good solution is a reproducible train→predict pipeline that maximizes classification accuracy and emits a Kaggle-ready submission matching sample_submission.csv.

deliverable_options.title: End-to-end Kaggle training + submission pipeline
deliverable_options.description: A CLI/script that trains on train.csv, writes OOF/CV metrics, predicts on test.csv, and produces a submission.csv with columns PassengerId,Transported (boolean or string matching the competition format). Includes preprocessing, feature engineering from Cabin/PassengerId/Name, and a tunable model.

deliverable_options.title: sklearn-compatible estimator package
deliverable_options.description: A fit/predict estimator (plus optional Pipeline) that can be cross-validated locally; a thin wrapper converts predictions into the Kaggle submission file.

deliverable_options.title: Single notebook baseline
deliverable_options.description: One self-contained notebook that explores, trains, and exports submission.csv with less emphasis on reusable CLI contracts.

metric_options.name: Accuracy
metric_options.rationale: Official Spaceship Titanic competition metric; submissions are scored by fraction of correct Transported labels.

metric_options.name: ROC-AUC (probability)
metric_options.rationale: Useful secondary metric for ranking/thresholding when the model outputs probabilities, but not what Kaggle ranks.

metric_options.name: Log loss
metric_options.rationale: Penalizes poorly calibrated probabilities; good for model selection but diverges from the official accuracy leaderboard.

protocol.quick: Stratified k-fold (e.g. 5-fold) CV on train.csv only, reporting mean±std accuracy. Optionally group folds by PassengerId group prefix to reduce within-group leakage. Agent may see full train labels and CV scores; keep no held-out slice at this stage.
protocol.validation: Hold out a fixed stratified (or group-aware) validation split from train.csv that the agent never tunes against iteratively as a pseudo-leaderboard; evaluate accuracy once after model selection on CV. Hide this holdout's labels from repeated agent feedback to limit overfitting to a small local set.
protocol.final: Train on all train.csv (or CV-chosen config), predict test.csv, write submission.csv, and score via Kaggle API for competition slug spaceship-titanic. Keep Kaggle public/private leaderboard labels fully hidden from the agent; only return the public score (and optionally private if available) as the final metric. Do not join test labels from any source.

questions.question: How should cross-validation treat PassengerId groups (families sharing a group id)?
options: GroupKFold / group-aware stratified folds by PassengerId group (recommended)
questions.default: GroupKFold / group-aware stratified folds by PassengerId group (recommended)

questions.question: Preferred model family for the search?
options: sklearn ensembles / logistic / RF only (no boosting deps)

questions.question: How should Transported be written in submission.csv?
options: Either is fine if Kaggle accepts it

questions.question: Compute budget for hyperparameter search?
options: Light: few models, default-ish params, minutes (recommended)
Medium: modest Optuna/grid search, tens of minutes
questions.default: Light: few models, default-ish params, minutes (recommended)

risks: Group leakage: passengers in the same PassengerId group (and often Cabin/Name patterns) are correlated; random CV can overstate accuracy.
Missing values and mixed types (CryoSleep/VIP as object/bool, Cabin/Name as high-cardinality strings) can break naive pipelines or create target leakage if filled with target statistics improperly.
Tiny-to-medium data (~8.7k train) means noisy local accuracy and easy overfitting to public LB via repeated submissions.
Amenity spends and CryoSleep are strong signals; poor imputation or treating CryoSleep inconsistently can swing accuracy several points.
